nodes.name: Proof Technique
nodes.statement: : We bound W_2(pi_k,pi_infty) leq W_2(pi_k,nu_kepsilon) + W_2(nu_kepsilon,pi_infty), where nu_kepsilon is the measure, at time kepsilon, of a particular continuous time diffusion with stationary measure pi_infty. We obtain W_2(pi_k,nu_kepsilon) leq O(kepsilonsqrtepsilon) through a Girsanov change of measure technique and a weighted transportation cost inequality. We then show that the diffusion satisfies a logarithmic-Sobolev inequality, allowing us to employ exponential decay of entropy and the Otto-Villani Theorem to show exponential decay of W_2(nu_kepsilon,pi_infty). This proof structure is mirrored in the seminal work . However, our algorithm necessitates a non-trivial extension of the methods in ; we utilize both a generalized stochastic gradient Langevin dynamics form and a weighting kernel to control the external gradient evaluations. The generalized form disrupts absolute continuity of measure between the algorithm and continuous time diffusion, necessitating the introduction and control of an intermediate process in order to apply Girsanov's Theorem. It also necessitates control of the "sampling distribution" (from which initial SGD and PSGLD points are taken) to decrease discretization error. However, this control simultaneously increases a relative entropy term appearing in the final 2-Wasserstein bound; this is handled by a careful specification of other algorithmic parameters. Finally, the continuous time diffusion is also distinct from that in , so we must prove logarithmic-Sobolev inequality satisfaction by a novel Lyapunov function. Furthermore, there are a variety of supporting lemmas, such as exponential integrability of the generalized diffusion, which are required for our analysis. colorblack The proof of the subsequent L^1 cost reconstruction bound utilizes a uniform concentration inequality for multi-dimensional nonparametric kernel density estimators and a relation between the 2-Wasserstein distance and a negative order Sobolev norm , which can be translated to the L^1 distance.

: We bound $\mathcal{W}_2(\pi_{k},\pi_{\infty}) \leq \mathcal{W}_2(\pi_{k},
u_{k\epsilon}) + \mathcal{W}_2(
u_{k\epsilon},\pi_{\infty})$, where $
u_{k\epsilon}$ is the measure, at time $k\epsilon$, of a particular continuous time diffusion with stationary measure $\pi_{\infty}$. We obtain $\mathcal{W}_2(\pi_{k},
u_{k\epsilon}) \leq \mathcal{O}(k\epsilon\sqrt{\epsilon})$ through a Girsanov change of measure technique and a weighted transportation cost inequality. We then show that the diffusion satisfies a logarithmic-Sobolev inequality, allowing us to employ exponential decay of entropy and the Otto-Villani Theorem to show exponential decay of $\mathcal{W}_2(
u_{k\epsilon},\pi_{\infty})$. This proof structure is mirrored in the seminal work \cite{raginsky2017non}. However, our algorithm necessitates a  non-trivial extension of the methods in \cite{raginsky2017non}; we utilize both a generalized stochastic gradient Langevin dynamics form and a weighting kernel to control the external gradient evaluations. The generalized form disrupts absolute continuity of measure between the algorithm and continuous time diffusion, necessitating the introduction and control of an intermediate process in order to apply Girsanov's Theorem. It also necessitates control of the "sampling distribution" (from which initial SGD and PSGLD points are taken) to decrease discretization error. However, this control simultaneously increases a relative entropy term appearing in the final 2-Wasserstein bound; this is handled by a careful specification of other algorithmic parameters. Finally, the continuous time diffusion is also distinct from that in \cite{raginsky2017non}, so we must prove logarithmic-Sobolev inequality satisfaction by a novel Lyapunov function. Furthermore, there are a variety of supporting lemmas, such as exponential integrability of the generalized diffusion, which are required for our analysis.

{\color{black} The proof of the subsequent $L^1$ cost reconstruction bound utilizes a uniform concentration inequality for multi-dimensional nonparametric kernel density estimators \cite{vogel2013uniform} and a relation between the 2-Wasserstein distance and a negative order Sobolev norm \cite{peyre2018comparison}, which can be translated to the $L^1$ distance.}

Begin by expanding the definition of 2-Wasserstein distance 
\begin{align*}
\mathcal{W}_2(\mu,\nu) &= \inf_{\gamma \in \Gamma(\mu,\nu)}\left( \int_{\Theta \times \Theta}\|x-y\|^2d\gamma(x,y) + \int_{(\Theta \times \Theta)^C}\|x-y\|^2d\gamma(x,y)\right)^{1/2}\\ 
&\geq \inf_{\gamma \in \Gamma(\mu,\nu)}\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\left(\sqrt{\int_{\Theta \times \Theta}\|x-y\|^2d\gamma(x,y)} + \sqrt{\int_{(\Theta \times \Theta)^C}\|x-y\|^2d\gamma(x,y)} \right) \\
&\geq \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\left(\inf_{\gamma \in \Gamma(\mu,\nu)}\sqrt{\int_{\Theta \times \Theta}\| x-y\|^2d\gamma(x,y)} + \sqrt{\int_{(\Theta \times \Theta)^C}\|x-y\|^2d\tilde{\gamma}(x,y)}\right) \\
&\geq \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\left(\inf_{\gamma \in \Gamma(\hat{\mu},\hat{\nu})}\sqrt{\int_{\Theta \times \Theta}\xi\|x-y\|^2d\gamma(x,y)} + \sqrt{\int_{(\Theta \times \Theta)^C}\|x-y\|^2d\tilde{\gamma}(x,y)}\right)
\end{align*}

\label{lem:otsubset}
Consider probability densities $\mu$, $\nu$ on $\mathbb{R}^{N}$ and compact subsets $\Theta',\Theta \subset \mathbb{R}^{N}$. Denote $\partial\Omega$ the boundary of set $\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^{N}$. Suppose the following properties, with $\alpha,\kappa > 0, \,\Delta > \sqrt{\frac{\kappa}{\alpha}}$, are satisfied:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\roman*)]
    \item $\int_{\Theta'} \mu(x)dx \geq \alpha$
    \item $\mathcal{W}_2(\mu,\nu) \leq \kappa$
    \item $\Theta' \subset \Theta \subset \mathbb{R}^{N}$,  $\inf_{x\in\partial\Theta,y\in\partial\Theta'}\|x-y\| \geq \Delta$
\end{enumerate}

Let $\hat{\gamma}$ denote the optimal transport measure coupling $\mu$ and $\nu$ \eqref{def:wass},
\[\hat{\gamma} \in \arg\inf_{\gamma\in\Gamma(\mu,\nu)}\left(\int_{\mathbb{R}^{N}\times\mathbb{R}^{N}}\|x-y\|^2d\gamma(x,y)\right)^{1/2}\]
Then, we have that $\int_{\Theta\times\Theta}d\hat{\gamma}(x,y) \geq (\alpha - \kappa\Delta^{-2})^2$

nodes.statement: Let V be the total density transported from mu in Theta' to nu in R^N/Theta under transportation map hatgamma. It is well known, under the Monge optimal transport reformulation, that the non-degenerate joint measure hatgamma is equivalent to a map T: R^N to R^N, such that int_R^NtimesR^N\|x-y\|^2dhatgamma(x,y) = int_R^N\|x-T(x)\|^2mu(x)d(x), \, T_*(mu) = nu, where T_*(mu) is the push-forward of mu. It can be seen that, given (iii), V is maximized under a geometry where inf_yinpartialTheta\|x-y\| = Delta\,forall xin partialTheta', a transport map T such that T(x) = inf_yinpartialTheta\|x-y\| \, forall xin Omega subseteq Theta', \,T(x) = x \, forall cinR^N/Omega. Here Omega is taken necessarily small enough so that int_R^N\|x-T(x)\|^2mu(x)d(x) = int_Omega\|x-T(x)\|^2mu(x)d(x) leq kappa^2 by (ii). Then, for any xinOmega, we have \|x-T(x)\|geq Delta and V = int_Omegamu(x)d(x) leq kappaDelta^-2. Thus, letting zeta = argmin_betain\mu,nu\int_Thetadbeta(x), we have int_Theta times Thetadhatgamma(x,y) geq left(int_Thetadzeta(x)right)^2 geq (alpha - kappaDelta^-2)^2 by the previous reasoning and (i).

nodes.statement: Eleft[\|pi_0,gamma(alpha_k)\|^2right] = int_0^inftyPleft( pi_0,gamma^2(alpha_k) > xright)dx We define the level set \[Delta_x^gamma := \yinR^N : pi_0,gamma^2(y) > x\\] so that \[Pleft(pi_0,gamma^2(alpha_k) > xright) = P(alpha_k in Delta_x^gamma)\] Now split this term as P(alpha_k in Delta_x^gamma) &= P(alpha_k in Delta_x^gamma | alpha_k-1 in Delta_x^gamma)P(alpha_k-1 in Delta_x^gamma) \\& + P(alpha_k in Delta_x^gamma | alpha_k-1 notin Delta_x^gamma)P(alpha_k-1 notin Delta_x^gamma) \\ & leq P(alpha_k in Delta_x^gamma | alpha_k-1 in Delta_x^gamma) + P(alpha_k in Delta_x^gamma | alpha_k-1 notin Delta_x^gamma) Now, from , denote \[nabla_k := epsilonbiggl[Kleft(fractheta_k -alpha_kDeltaright) fracbeta2 hatnabla J (theta_k) + nabla pi_0,gamma(alpha_k)biggr]pi_0,gamma(alpha_k), tildew_k := sqrtepsilonpi_0,gamma(alpha_k) w_k\] so that tildew_k sim N(0,epsilonpi_0,gamma(alpha_k)^2). Then observe that, given tildew_k is symmetric with mean zero, P(alpha_k in Delta_x^gamma | alpha_k-1 in Delta_x^gamma) &= P(alpha_k-1 - nabla_k-1 + tildew_k in Delta_x^gamma | alpha_k-1 in Delta_x^gamma) \\&leq P(alpha_k in Delta_x^gamma | alpha_k-1 - nabla_k-1 in Delta_x^gamma) Similarly, P(alpha_k in Delta_x^gamma | alpha_k-1 notin Delta_x^gamma) leq P(alpha_k in Delta_x^gamma | alpha_k-1 - nabla_k in Delta_x^gamma) so that \[P(alpha_k in Delta_x^gamma) leq 2P(alpha_k in Delta_x^gamma | alpha_k-1 - nabla_k-1 in Delta_x^gamma)\] Now, let zeta_z^epsilon,gamma := (epsilon pi_0,gamma^2(z))^-1, define \[hatDelta_x^gamma(z) := \yin R^N : y/z in Delta_x^gamma \\] and notice that &Pleft(alpha_k in Delta_x^gamma | alpha_k-1 - nabla_k-1 in Delta_x^gammaright) \\& = Pleft(zeta_alpha_k-1^epsilon,gammaalpha_k in hatDelta_x^gamma(zeta_alpha_k-1^epsilon,gamma) \,| \,zeta_alpha_k-1^epsilon,gammaalpha_k-1 - zeta_alpha_k-1^epsilon,gammanabla_k-1 in hatDelta_x^gamma(zeta_alpha_k-1^epsilon,gamma)right) \\ & = Pbiggl(zeta_alpha_k-1^epsilon,gamma(alpha_k-1 - nabla_k-1 + sqrtepsilon pi_0,gamma(alpha_k-1) w_k) in hatDelta_x^gamma(zeta_alpha_k-1^epsilon,gamma) \, | \\& zeta_alpha_k-1^epsilon,gamma( alpha_k-1 - nabla_k-1) in hatDelta_x^gamma(zeta_alpha_k-1^epsilon,gamma) biggr) Then, since zeta_alpha_k-1^epsilon,gamma sqrtepsilon pi_0,gamma(alpha_k-1) w_k sim N(0,(zeta_alpha_k-1^epsilon,gamma)^2 \,epsilon \,pi_0,gamma^2(alpha_k-1)) we have that, &Pleft(alpha_k in Delta_x^gamma | alpha_k-1 - nabla_k-1 in Delta_x^gammaright) \\& leq int_hatDelta_x^gamma(zeta_alpha_k-1^epsilon,gamma)N(gamma; hatc,(zeta_alpha_k-1^epsilon,gamma)^2\, epsilon \,pi_0,gamma^2(alpha_k-1))dgamma = int_hatDelta_x^gamma(zeta_alpha_k-1^epsilon,gamma)N(gamma; hatc,zeta_alpha_k-1^epsilon,gamma)dgamma Now, crucially, observe that the volume of hatDelta_x^gamma(zeta_z^epsilon,gamma) scales, w.r.t z, at the same rate as the variance of N(cdot,hatc,zeta_z^epsilon,gamma). Thus we have \[int_hatDelta_x^gamma(zeta^epsilon,gamma_z_1)N(gamma; hatc,zeta^epsilon,gamma_z_1 )dgamma = int_hatDelta_x^gamma(zeta^epsilon,gamma_z_2)N(gamma; hatc, zeta^epsilon,gamma_z_2)dgamma forall \, z_1,z_2 > 0\] In particular, take z such that zeta_z^epsilon,gamma = (epsilon pi_0,gamma^2(z))^-1 = epsilon^2. Note that this necessitates barpi_0,gamma geq (frac1epsilon)^3/2, which is given from the condition gamma leq barpi_0\,epsilon^3/2. Then we have Pleft(alpha_k in Delta_x^gamma | alpha_k-1 - nabla_k-1 in Delta_x^gammaright) &leq int_hatDelta_x^gamma(epsilon^2)N(gamma; hatc,epsilon^2)dgamma \\&leq int_hatDelta_x^gamma(epsilon^2)frac1epsilonsqrt2pidgamma = int_hatDelta_x^gamma(1)fracepsilonsqrt2pidgamma Then Eleft[\|pi_0,gamma(alpha_k)\|^2right] &= int_0^inftyP(pi_0,gamma^2(alpha_k) > x)dx\\ &leq 2int_0^inftyint_Delta_x^gammafracepsilonsqrt2pidgamma dx =sqrtfrac2piepsilonint_0^inftyint_R^Nmathds1\pi_0,gamma(gamma)>sqrtx\dgamma dx \\ but observe that, for gamma leq 1, \[int_0^inftyint_R^Nmathds1\pi_0,gamma(gamma)>sqrtx\dgamma\, dx leq int_0^inftyint_R^Nmathds1\pi_0(gamma)>sqrtx\dgamma \,dx\] So now Eleft[\|pi_0,gamma(alpha_k)\|^2right] &leq sqrtfrac2piepsilonint_0^inftyint_R^Nmathds1\pi_0(gamma)>sqrtx\dgamma \,dx \\ &= sqrtfrac2piepsilonbiggl[int_0^1int_R^Nmathds1\pi_0(gamma)>sqrtx\dgamma \,dx \\& + int_1^barpi_0,gamma^2int_R^Nmathds1\pi_0(gamma)>sqrtx\dgamma \,dxbiggr] \\&leq sqrtfrac2piepsilonbiggl[int_0^1int_R^Nmathds1\pi_0(gamma)> x\dgamma \,dx + barpi_0,gamma^2\,V(\pi_0 > 1\)biggr] \\ &leq epsilonleft[1 + V(\pi_0>1\)right] =: epsilon V_1 where V(\pi_0>1\) is shorthand for int_R^Nmathds1\pi_0(gamma)>1\dgamma. Define, analagously, \[Gamma_x^gamma = \y in R^N : \|nablapi_0,gamma(y)\|^2 > x\\] By the same procedure as above, we can obtain \[P(alpha_k in Gamma_x^gamma) leq 2int_Gamma_x^gammafracepsilonsqrt2pidgamma\] and so E\|nablapi_0,gamma(alpha_k)\|^2 &= int_0^inftyP(\|nablapi_0,gamma(alpha_k)\|^2 > x)dx leq 2int_0^inftyint_Gamma_x^gammasqrtfrac2piepsilon dgamma dx \\ &leq epsilonleft[ 1 + barpi_0' V(\\|nablapi_0\|>1\)right] =:epsilon V_2 where barpi_0' = sup_xinR^Nnablapi_0(x), V(\\|nablapi_0\|>1\) = int_R^Nmathds1\\|nablapi_0(gamma)\|>1\dgamma. Taking pi_0 such that barpi_0 = 1 gives \[ Eleft[\|pi_0,gamma(alpha_k)\|^2right] leq epsilon, E\|nablapi_0,gamma(alpha_k)\|^2 leq epsilon\]

Then we have Pleft(alpha_k in Delta_x^gamma | alpha_k-1 - nabla_k-1 in Delta_x^gammaright) &leq int_hatDelta_x^gamma(epsilon^2)N(gamma; hatc,epsilon^2)dgamma \\&leq int_hatDelta_x^gamma(epsilon^2)frac1epsilonsqrt2pidgamma = int_hatDelta_x^gamma(1)fracepsilonsqrt2pidgamma Then Eleft[\|pi_0,gamma(alpha_k)\|^2right] &= int_0^inftyP(pi_0,gamma^2(alpha_k) > x)dx\\ &leq 2int_0^inftyint_Delta_x^gammafracepsilonsqrt2pidgamma dx =sqrtfrac2piepsilonint_0^inftyint_R^Nmathds1\pi_0,gamma(gamma)>sqrtx\dgamma dx \\ but observe that, for gamma leq 1, \[int_0^inftyint_R^Nmathds1\pi_0,gamma(gamma)>sqrtx\dgamma\, dx leq int_0^inftyint_R^Nmathds1\pi_0(gamma)>sqrtx\dgamma \,dx\] So now Eleft[\|pi_0,gamma(alpha_k)\|^2right] &leq sqrtfrac2piepsilonint_0^inftyint_R^Nmathds1\pi_0(gamma)>sqrtx\dgamma \,dx \\ &= sqrtfrac2piepsilonbiggl[int_0^1int_R^Nmathds1\pi_0(gamma)>sqrtx\dgamma \,dx \\& + int_1^barpi_0,gamma^2int_R^Nmathds1\pi_0(gamma)>sqrtx\dgamma \,dxbiggr] \\&leq sqrtfrac2piepsilonbiggl[int_0^1int_R^Nmathds1\pi_0(gamma)> x\dgamma \,dx + barpi_0,gamma^2\,V(\pi_0 > 1\)biggr] \\ &leq epsilonleft[1 + V(\pi_0>1\)right] =: epsilon V_1 where V(\pi_0>1\) is shorthand for int_R^Nmathds1\pi_0(gamma)>1\dgamma. Define, analagously, \[Gamma_x^gamma = \y in R^N : \|nablapi_0,gamma(y)\|^2 > x\\] By the same procedure as above, we can obtain \[P(alpha_k in Gamma_x^gamma) leq 2int_Gamma_x^gammafracepsilonsqrt2pidgamma\] and so E\|nablapi_0,gamma(alpha_k)\|^2 &= int_0^inftyP(\|nablapi_0,gamma(alpha_k)\|^2 > x)dx leq 2int_0^inftyint_Gamma_x^gammasqrtfrac2piepsilon dgamma dx \\ &leq epsilonleft[ 1 + barpi_0' V(\\|nablapi_0\|>1\)right] =:epsilon V_2 where barpi_0' = sup_xinR^Nnablapi_0(x), V(\\|nablapi_0\|>1\) = int_R^Nmathds1\\|nablapi_0(gamma)\|>1\dgamma. Taking pi_0 such that barpi_0 = 1 gives \[ Eleft[\|pi_0,gamma(alpha_k)\|^2right] leq epsilon, E\|nablapi_0,gamma(alpha_k)\|^2 leq epsilon\]

nodes.statement: First note that for all xin R^N we have nablapi_0,gamma(x) = fracnablapi_0(x)gamma, so \[argmax_yinR^N\|langle y,\, nabla pi_0,gamma(y) rangle\| = argmax_yinR^N\|langle gamma y,\, fracnabla pi_0(y)gamma rangle\| = argmax_yinR^N\|langle y,\, nabla pi_0(y) rangle\|\] and &argmax_yinR^N\|langle y,\, pi_0,gamma(y)nabla pi_0,gamma(y) rangle\| = argmax_yinR^N\|langle gamma y,\, pi_0,gamma(y)fracnabla pi_0(y)gamma rangle\|\\& = argmax_yinR^N\|langle y,\, pi_0(y)nabla pi_0(y) rangle\| Thus is equivalent to: &exists I >0 : \|langle x, nablapi_0(x) rangle\| leq I \ forall x in R^N &exists I' >0 : \|langle x, pi_0(x)nablapi_0(x) rangle\| leq I' \ forall x in R^N Now we prove by reductio ad absurdum: Suppose , do not hold. Then we have: &forall y >0 \ exists x in R^N : \ \|langle x, nablapi_0(x) rangle\| > y \\ &forall y >0 \ exists x in R^N : \ \|langle x, pi_0(x)nablapi_0(x) rangle\| > y Recall M as defined in Assumption~. Denote \[D_1 = \xin R^N : \|x\| leq M vee 1\, \,D_2 = D_1^C = R^Nbackslash D_1\] Recall that we assume Lipshitz-continuity of pi_0(cdot) in (), with Lipschitz constant L_pi_0. Thus, \|nablapi_0(x)\| is bounded by L_pi_0 for all xinR^N. In particular notice that since \|nablapi_0(x)\|, \|pi_0(x)\|, and \|x\| are bounded for x in D_1, there exists some M^*,M^** such that \[\|langle x, nablapi_0(x) rangle\| leq M^* \ forall x in D_1\] \[\|langle x, pi_0(x)nablapi_0(x) rangle\| leq M^** \ forall x in D_1\] Then requires both: &forall y > M^* \ exists x in D_2 : \ \|langle x, nabla pi_0(x) rangle\| > y \\ &forall y > M^** \ exists x in D_2 : \ \|langle x, nabla pi_0(x)nablapi_0(x) rangle\| > y But by assumption~ nabla pi_0(x) decays as O(\|x\|^-1) for x in D_2, and in Lemma~ pi_0(x) decays as O(\|x\|^-2). Specifically, there exists tildeC such that \[\|nablapi_0(x)\| leq fractildeC\|x\|^-1, \|pi_0(x)\| leq frac2(beta m^*)^2\|x\|^2,\, forall x in D_2\] Thus we have that \[\|langle x, nabla pi_0(x) rangle\| leq tildeC \ forall x in D_2\] \[\|langle x, pi_0(x)nabla pi_0(x) rangle\| leq frac2tildeC(beta m^*)^2 \ forall x in D_2\]which contradicts and thus is refuted. So holds.

nodes.statement: colorblackConsider the Theta-restricted distributions barpi_k,barpi_infty, given by \[barpi_k(x) = pi_k(x)/Z_pi_k \, &xin Theta \\ 0, &xnotin Theta , Z_pi_k := int_Thetapi_k(x)dx\] \[barpi_infty(x) = pi_infty(x)/Z_pi_infty \, &xin Theta \\ 0, &xnotin Theta , Z_pi_infty := int_Thetapi_infty(x)dx,\] where Z_pi_k and Z_pi_infty are normalizing constants. We begin by showing that the sampling scheme in Algorithm~ produces i.i.d. samples from a measure barpi such that colorblackW_2(barpi,barpi_infty) leq sqrt2xi^-1rho, where xi is defined in . First observe that by our choice of delta, we have \[deltaleft[C_4 + sqrt2c_LS C_3 right] + deltasqrt10c_LSNlogleft(1/deltaright) leq rho \] and thus, with epsilon leq left(fracdeltalog(1/delta) right)^2 and hatk taken as we have W_2(pi_hatk,pi_infty) leq rho by Theorem~, and W_2(barpi_hatk,barpi_infty) leq sqrt2xi^-1rho by Lemma~. textcolorblackNow observe (by Lemma~) that the empirical sample set S = cup_i=1^|S|alpha_hatk^i from Algorithm~ is composed of i.i.d. samples. This, along with Assumption~ and , allows us to employ Theorem 2 of to derive: Pleft(sup_thetainR^N|hatpi(theta) - barpi_hatk(theta)| geq beta_x,T right) leq H(x) where beta_x,T = fracxsqrt|S|b_S + fracK_2(2pi) ^Nsqrt|S|b_S + frac12K_3K_4b_S^2/N, H(x) = 2e^frac-x^22K_1^2 Then, since b_S = b_TsqrtfracT|S|, we have beta_x,T = fracxsqrtTb_T + fracK_2(2pi) ^NsqrtTb_T + frac12K_3K_4left(b_TsqrtfracT|S|right)^2/N, H(x) = 2e^frac-x^22K_1^2 Next we utilize a result of which allows us to bound the L^1 distance between barpi_hatk(cdot) and barpi_infty in terms of the 2-Wasserstein bound already achieved. Specifically, defining the negative-order Sobolev norm \[\|f\|^2_dotH^1 = int_R^N\|nabla f(x)\|^2 dx\] and for a measure mu on R^N the dual norm \[\|mu\|_dotH^-1 = supleft\|langle f,murangle| bigg|\|f\|_dotH^1 leq 1right\\] and given measures mu,nu on R^N, bounded by C < infty, we have \|mu - nu\|_dotH^-1 leq sqrtCW_2(mu,nu). textcolorblackNow consider the following bounds on barpi_hatk(theta) and barpi_infty. Let T_1 denote an upper bound on J in sampling region Theta (this exists by ). Then, we have sup_thetainR^Nbarpi_infty(theta) leq (exp(-beta T_1)|Theta|)^-1 Notice now that by construction we can produce an upper bound on hatpi as sup_theta in R^Nhatpi(theta) leq fracK_1b_S = fracK_1b_T sqrtT/|S| leq fracK_1b_T. Then, using we may produce the concentration bound: Pleft(sup_thetainR^Nbarpi_hatk (theta) leq fracK_1b_T + beta_x,Tright) geq 1-H(x) In particular, textcolorblackletting C_6 = left(fracK_1b_T + beta_x,Tright) vee left( frac1exp(-beta T_1 |Theta|)right) with probability at least 1-H(x) we have \|barpi_hatk(theta) - barpi_infty(theta)\|_1 = int_Theta| barpi_hatk(theta) - barpi_infty(theta)| dtheta = |langle 1, barpi_hatk - barpi_inftyrangle | leq \|barpi_hatk - barpi_infty\|_dotH^-1 leq sqrtC_6W_2(barpi_hatk,barpi_infty) leq sqrtfrac2xiC_6 rho This will be useful for us momentarily. Now observe, since J is bounded, we can enforce Lipschitz-continuity of the logarithmic transformation (\|log(x) - log(y)\| leq L\|x-y\| \, forall x,y geq exp(-beta T_1)), to obtain textcolorblack &Pleft(int_Theta|hatJ(theta) - J(theta)|dtheta geq phi_x,textcolorblackTright) leq Pleft(int_Theta|hatpi(theta) - barpi_infty(theta)|dtheta geq phi_x,textcolorblackT/Lright) \\ &overset1leq Pleft(int_Theta|hatpi(theta) - barpi_hatk(theta)|dtheta + int_Theta|barpi_hatk(theta) - barpi_infty(theta)| dtheta geq phi_x,textcolorblackT/L right) \\ & overset2leq Pleft(int_Theta|hatpi(theta) - barpi_hatk(theta)|dtheta + int_Theta|barpi_hatk(theta) - barpi_infty(theta)| dtheta geq phi_x,T/L bigg| int_Theta|barpi_hatk(theta) - barpi_infty(theta)| dtheta leq sqrtC_6W_2(barpi_hatk, barpi_infty)right)\\ & cdot Pleft(int_Theta|barpi_hatk(theta) - barpi_infty(theta)| dtheta leq sqrtC_6W_2(barpi_hatk,barpi_infty)right)\\ & + Pleft(int_Theta|hatpi(theta) - barpi_infty(theta)| dtheta geq sqrtC_6W_2(barpi_hatk,barpi_infty)right)\\ & leq Pleft(int_Theta|hatpi(theta) - barpi_hatk(theta)|dtheta + sqrtC_6W_2(barpi_hatk, barpi_infty) geq phi_x,T/L right) + Pleft(int_Theta|barpi_hatk(theta) - b) + fracm beta Ibarpi_0,gamma^2+1 pi_0,gamma(x) \\ & + frac12pi_0,gamma^2(x)(fracm beta Nbarpi_0,gamma^2+1 + (fracmbetabarpi_0,gamma^2+1)^2\|x\|^2))biggr\V(x)\\ & leq biggl\biggl(frac12 beta m N + m beta I + frac12pi_0,gamma^2(x) fracbeta^2 m bbarpi_0,gamma^2+1biggr) \\& -
